subject: Breach-notice-window-and-SCC-cooperation-language - proposal
messages:
From: Paul Hart <paul.hart@northpointhealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: legal@northpointhealth.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Alignment on notification window + SCC cooperation obligations

Jordan —

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As we start redlining the draft DPA, Legal at Northpoint asked me to put the key ask in writing so we have a single thread for review. Two items we're trying to align on:

1) Notification window for security incidents impacting personal data. For HIPAA-covered data we generally need a tight turnaround; our baseline is 48 hours for initial notification and a 72-hour follow-up with a preliminary impact summary.

2) Cooperation under the standard contractual clauses (SCCs) — specifically: the scope of evidence you can provide (logs, audit trails), timelines for preservation requests, and whether Redwood will provide operational support for DPIA-related inquiries.

Can you confirm Redwood's proposed notification timing and suggest language we can include in the SCC/coop clause? If you can attach a short redline or clause draft that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — we hope to close DPA language this month.

Best,
Paul
Paul Hart
Head of Compliance Programs
Northpoint Health

Attachments: Northpoint_SCCs_annotated.pdf (pdf)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Paul Hart <paul.hart@northpointhealth.com>
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 13:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Alignment on notification window + SCC cooperation obligations

Paul —

Thanks for the clear summary. Looping in Mina (Legal) and Rishi (Security) so we can propose precise contract language and confirm operational feasibility. Quick answers up front:

- Initial notification: Redwood can commit to an initial notification within 48 hours for incidents involving regulated personal data (including HIPAA PHI), provided we have actionable evidence that a confidentiality or integrity event has occurred.
- Preliminary impact summary: we can aim for a 72-hour preliminary summary, but we will flag any blockers if we require forensic time.
- SCC cooperation: we can provide logs/metadata and a redacted timeline of events. Full packet captures or raw patient records cannot be shared. We can accept preservation requests and aim to fulfill them within 5 business days depending on scope.

Attached is a first-pass clause for the DPA incident section — short, contract-ready, and intended to be vendor-friendly while addressing common customer needs. Mina: please review and tighten the legalese as needed. Rishi: flag any operational dependencies (for example, whether a 48-hour initial notice requires on-call escalation).

Next steps: Mina will propose a redline, and Rishi will confirm the engineering runbook and expected time-to-evidence. Happy to jump on a 30-minute sync if Northpoint wants to walk through specifics.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Proposed_DPA_Incident_Clause_v1.docx (docx)
From: Northpoint Legal <legal@northpointhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Hart <paul.hart@northpointhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Alignment on notification window + SCC cooperation obligations

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the proposal and for including the operational caveats. A couple of comments from Legal after a quick read of the draft clause:

- We'd like the initial notification window to be explicit: 48 hours for initial acknowledgement and 48 additional hours for a preliminary impact summary (i.e., 96 hours total), rather than 72 hours. Our internal HIPAA playbooks assume two distinct checkpoints.
- Preservation requests: we need a firm timeline of 3 business days for preservation of logs/metadata when invoked by an authorized security contact (we can provide a template). If there is a forensic hold, Northpoint requires a named point of contact at Redwood and weekly status updates.
- SCC cooperation: we note the limitation on raw datasets; however, for DPIA support we need a commitment to provide pseudonymized extracts or synthetic samples when feasible, and a scope-limited extraction plan within 10 business days.

Can Mina/legal on your side confirm acceptance or propose middle ground? We would prefer to avoid escalation to procurement.

Regards,
Northpoint Legal

Attachment: Northpoint_SCCs_annotated.pdf (pdf)
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Northpoint Legal <legal@northpointhealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Alignment on notification window + SCC cooperation obligations

Hi Paul / Northpoint Legal —

Appreciate the specificity; this is very helpful. Quick responses to each bullet and a proposed compromise:

- Initial notification: Redwood accepts a firm 48-hour acknowledgement for incidents involving regulated personal data. For the preliminary impact summary, Redwood proposes 72 hours for the first substantive update. If Northpoint requires two formal checkpoints (48 + 48), we can add a 48-hour acknowledgement plus a 96-hour preliminary report for contract language, but we ask that the clause include a reasonableness exception for complex forensic work. Suggested language: "Vendor will provide initial acknowledgement within 48 hours of discovery and use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver a preliminary impact summary within 96 hours; if additional forensic analysis is required, Vendor will notify Customer of the expected completion date and provide weekly status updates."

- Preservation timeline: Redwood can commit to preserving logs/metadata within 3 business days upon receipt of an authorized preservation request. We'll include a requirement for a named customer contact and a scope template.

- DPIA support / extracts: Redwood will provide pseudonymized extracts or scoped synthetic samples when feasible within 10 business days of a formal request, subject to technical feasibility and applicable law (e.g., if data is irreversibly encrypted or controlled by customer consent constraints).

Operational note (Rishi): to meet the 48-hour initial notice consistently will require an updated on-call escalation (we will document the SLA path and the runbook). We will attach a short appendix describing the evidence types we can deliver and the typical timelines.

If that compromise works, Mina will push a redline to your doc and Jordan will coordinate the next steps for signature. Happy to set a 30-minute legal ops call next week to finalize.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

--
Rishi Malhotra (on behalf of Security Operations)
Head of Security Operations — Redwood Inference
